Implementing RRP: A Simulated Hospital Walkthrough

Source: vignettes/articles/implementing-rrp.Rmd
implementing-rrp.Rmd

A hospital’s changing question

Harbor General wants to reassess patients after they leave the hospital. A prediction made at discharge cannot use observations collected later. It also does not, by itself, answer how much risk remains several days into follow-up. Readmission Risk Pool (RRP) lets the hospital assess that remaining risk at chosen times, keep each result, and examine the current pool and earlier estimates. The readmit package supplies this workflow; the hospital supplies its source mapping and risk model.

For an eligible discharge episode, the target is the probability of a first readmission strictly after the assessment time and through 30 elapsed days after the original discharge. The 30-day endpoint stays fixed even when the hospital assesses an episode again. An estimate may change as less time remains or as the hospital gains new information for its model; it need not move in a particular direction. A readmission or death occurring by the assessment time makes an episode ineligible for a new remaining-risk estimate.

Everything here is simulated for teaching. The model is neither clinically validated nor evidence that acting on its estimates improves outcomes. Run the article with readmit, dplyr, and tidyr installed; its website build also uses rmarkdown and pkgdown. Once those packages are installed, the article requires no network, hospital connection, external dataset, or prepared model.

Simulate Harbor General’s extracts

We create a larger historical group of patients to train an illustrative model, then use eight separate current encounters to show how that model would be used in repeated assessments. Different discharge dates let patients enter the assessed population at different times. Readmissions and deaths show when a patient can no longer receive a new remaining-risk estimate. One patient has missing information, so the model cannot estimate that patient’s risk.

The tables resemble patient demographics, encounter and discharge records, post-discharge observations, and readmission and death records. An observation is recorded four days after discharge but becomes available to the hospital a day later. The hospital uses that availability time to choose private model inputs; the platform uses event occurrence time to decide eligibility.

Show simulated source-data preparation 
set.seed(6404)
day <- 24 * 60 * 60
origin <- as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
n_history <- 420L

historical_patients <- tibble(
  patient_id = sprintf("H%03d", seq_len(n_history)),
  age = sample(45:88, n_history, replace = TRUE)
)
historical_encounters <- tibble(
  encounter_id = sprintf("EH%03d", seq_len(n_history)),
  patient_id = historical_patients$patient_id,
  admission_time = origin - (80 - sample(0:20, n_history, replace = TRUE)) * day,
  acuity = sample(0:2, n_history, replace = TRUE),
  cohort = "historical"
) |>
  mutate(discharge_time = admission_time + sample(2:5, n_history, replace = TRUE) * day)
historical_observations <- historical_encounters |>
  transmute(
    encounter_id,
    signal = rbinom(n(), 1, plogis(-0.3 + 0.4 * acuity)),
    observed_at = discharge_time + 4 * day,
    available_at = discharge_time + 5 * day
  )

# Simulate later readmission and death outcomes for the historical cohort.
readmit_probability <- plogis(
  -2 + 0.025 * (historical_patients$age - 65) +
    0.35 * historical_encounters$acuity + 0.45 * historical_observations$signal
)
readmit_day <- ifelse(
  runif(n_history) < readmit_probability,
  sample(4:27, n_history, replace = TRUE), NA_integer_
)
death_day <- ifelse(
  runif(n_history) < 0.06,
  sample(4:27, n_history, replace = TRUE), NA_integer_
)
# A death before a simulated readmission prevents that later readmission.
readmit_day[!is.na(death_day) & !is.na(readmit_day) &
              death_day < readmit_day] <- NA_integer_
historical_readmissions <- historical_encounters |>
  mutate(event_day = readmit_day) |>
  filter(!is.na(event_day)) |>
  transmute(
    event_id = paste0("HR-", encounter_id), encounter_id,
    event_type = "readmission",
    occurred_at = discharge_time + event_day * day
  )
historical_deaths <- historical_encounters |>
  mutate(event_day = death_day) |>
  filter(!is.na(event_day)) |>
  transmute(
    event_id = paste0("HD-", encounter_id), encounter_id,
    event_type = "death",
    occurred_at = discharge_time + event_day * day
  )

current_patients <- tibble(
  patient_id = paste0("C", 1:8),
  age = c(72, 64, 61, NA, 70, 58, 68, 77)
)
current_encounters <- tibble(
  encounter_id = paste0("E", 1:8),
  patient_id = current_patients$patient_id,
  discharge_time = origin + c(0, 2, 6, 1, -27, 8, 14, 0) * day,
  acuity = c(2, 1, 0, 2, 1, 1, 2, 0),
  cohort = "current"
) |>
  mutate(admission_time = discharge_time - 2 * day)
current_observations <- current_encounters |>
  transmute(
    encounter_id, signal = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0),
    observed_at = discharge_time + 4 * day,
    available_at = discharge_time + 5 * day
  )
current_events <- tibble(
  event_id = c("ER-E1", "ED-E2"),
  encounter_id = c("E1", "E2"),
  event_type = c("readmission", "death"),
  occurred_at = origin + c(8.5, 13) * day
)

patients <- bind_rows(historical_patients, current_patients)
encounters <- bind_rows(historical_encounters, current_encounters)
observations <- bind_rows(historical_observations, current_observations)
events <- bind_rows(historical_readmissions, historical_deaths, current_events)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(patients$patient_id),
  !anyDuplicated(encounters$encounter_id),
  !anyDuplicated(events$event_id),
  all(encounters$patient_id %in% patients$patient_id),
  all(events$encounter_id %in% encounters$encounter_id)
)

The current encounters and terminal events used below are:

current_encounters |>
  select(encounter_id, patient_id, discharge_time, acuity)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   encounter_id patient_id discharge_time      acuity
#>   <chr>        <chr>      <dttm>               <dbl>
#> 1 E1           C1         2026-01-01 00:00:00      2
#> 2 E2           C2         2026-01-03 00:00:00      1
#> 3 E3           C3         2026-01-07 00:00:00      0
#> 4 E4           C4         2026-01-02 00:00:00      2
#> 5 E5           C5         2025-12-05 00:00:00      1
#> 6 E6           C6         2026-01-09 00:00:00      1
#> 7 E7           C7         2026-01-15 00:00:00      2
#> 8 E8           C8         2026-01-01 00:00:00      0
current_events |>
  select(encounter_id, event_type, occurred_at)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   encounter_id event_type  occurred_at        
#>   <chr>        <chr>       <dttm>             
#> 1 E1           readmission 2026-01-09 12:00:00
#> 2 E2           death       2026-01-14 00:00:00

The first current readmission occurs on January 9; the other recorded event is a death. E4’s patient has no age. E4 can still be eligible under the platform’s rules, but the hospital’s model needs age and cannot produce a probability for that episode. The platform records the failed estimate rather than treating E4 as ineligible or assigning it zero risk. E5’s follow-up window has already closed by the first assessment. E3, E6, and E7 enter the supplied discharge population on different days.

Create a project and map the sources

rrp_project_init() creates an ordinary, editable project. Its two R scripts start as deliberate stubs: initialization does not supply a working hospital model or source connection. Harbor General must write the source mapper that translates its data into the package’s discharge-episode and terminal-event tables, and the provider that calculates risk for eligible episodes. We save simulated extracts inside this project only because Harbor General is fictional; a real organization would connect its own sources and control their access.

work_dir <- tempfile("harbor-general-")
dir.create(work_dir)
project <- rrp_project_init(file.path(work_dir, "harbor-rrp"), "harbor-general")
dir.create(file.path(project, "source"))
saveRDS(patients, file.path(project, "source", "patients.rds"))
saveRDS(encounters, file.path(project, "source", "encounters.rds"))
saveRDS(observations, file.path(project, "source", "observations.rds"))
saveRDS(events, file.path(project, "source", "events.rds"))
list.files(project)
#> [1] "_brand.yml"        "app"               "assets"           
#> [4] "R"                 "README.md"         "rrp-authoring.dcf"
#> [7] "rrp-project.dcf"   "source"

The project contains configuration and branding, R/produce-canonical.R for source mapping, R/calculate-risk.R for the hospital’s provider, and app/ for the project-owned Shiny interface. state/ and generated products appear only when we initialize history and refresh products later.

The mapper below reads the extracts, connects encounters to patients, and returns the two required tables. For each assessment date, it supplies the complete relevant group of current encounters discharged by that time: discharge_time <= as_of_time. Supplying only part of that group at a later assessment would leave patients out of the current view. The package derives each episode’s original 30-day endpoint and applies its eligibility rules; the hospital does not need to reproduce those rules in the mapper.

Show source-mapping code 
mapper_code <- r"---(
rrp_produce_canonical <- function(project_root, as_of_time) {
  source_dir <- file.path(project_root, "source")
  patients <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "patients.rds"))
  encounters <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "encounters.rds"))
  events <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "events.rds"))

  selected <- encounters |>
    dplyr::filter(cohort == "current", discharge_time <= as_of_time) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(patients, patient_id), by = "patient_id")
  discharge_episode <- selected |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      episode_id = paste0("episode-", encounter_id),
      patient_id,
      index_encounter_id = encounter_id,
      admission_time, discharge_time
    )
  terminal_event <- events |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(selected, encounter_id), by = "encounter_id") |>
    dplyr::filter(occurred_at <= as_of_time) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      terminal_event_id = event_id,
      episode_id = paste0("episode-", encounter_id),
      event_type, occurred_at
    )
  list(
    discharge_episode = as.data.frame(discharge_episode),
    terminal_event = as.data.frame(terminal_event)
  )
}
)---"
writeLines(mapper_code, file.path(project, "R", "produce-canonical.R"))

This example’s mapper also selects only events that have occurred by the assessment date. That builds a source snapshot: the January 9 readmission is present on January 10, while a later event first appears in a later snapshot. The platform itself uses occurrence time to decide whether a supplied event makes an episode ineligible. Age, acuity, and the post-discharge observation stay private to the hospital’s model rather than entering the shared tables.

Fit a remaining-risk demonstration model

We use the historical patients to teach a model to answer the same question asked during current assessments. For each historical discharge, we consider the patient at days 2, 7, and 14. Each of these assessment points is a landmark. A patient contributes a training row at a landmark only if a readmission or death has not already occurred. Once either event occurs, there is no remaining first-readmission risk to estimate at a later landmark.

For each row, the outcome asks whether a first readmission occurred strictly after that landmark and by the original day-30 endpoint, before a competing death. We learn the outcome from later records, but give the model only predictors available at the landmark. In particular, the hospital withholds the post-discharge observation until its own availability time. This is a small educational logistic model of the remaining interval, not a validated clinical prediction system. Repeated rows per encounter and a simplified source process do not establish calibrated risk or clinical usefulness.

Show model-training code 
historical_event_times <- events |>
  semi_join(historical_encounters, by = "encounter_id") |>
  select(encounter_id, event_type, occurred_at) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = event_type,
    values_from = occurred_at,
    names_glue = "{.value}_{event_type}"
  )

training <- tidyr::crossing(
  encounter_id = historical_encounters$encounter_id,
  landmark_day = c(2L, 7L, 14L)
) |>
  left_join(historical_encounters, by = "encounter_id") |>
  left_join(historical_patients, by = "patient_id") |>
  left_join(historical_observations |>
              select(encounter_id, signal, signal_available_at = available_at),
            by = "encounter_id") |>
  left_join(historical_event_times, by = "encounter_id") |>
  mutate(
    as_of_time = discharge_time + landmark_day * day,
    followup_end = discharge_time + 30 * day,
    age_scaled = (age - 65) / 10,
    days_remaining = 30 - landmark_day,
    signal_as_of = if_else(signal_available_at <= as_of_time, signal, 0L)
  ) |>
  filter(
    is.na(occurred_at_readmission) | occurred_at_readmission > as_of_time,
    is.na(occurred_at_death) | occurred_at_death > as_of_time
  ) |>
  mutate(
    outcome = as.integer(
      !is.na(occurred_at_readmission) &
        occurred_at_readmission > as_of_time &
        occurred_at_readmission <= followup_end &
        (is.na(occurred_at_death) |
           occurred_at_readmission <= occurred_at_death)
    )
  )
model <- stats::glm(
  outcome ~ age_scaled + acuity + signal_as_of + days_remaining,
  family = stats::binomial(), data = training
)
dir.create(file.path(project, "model"))
model_path <- file.path(project, "model", "landmark-glm.rds")
saveRDS(model, model_path)
stopifnot(inherits(readRDS(model_path), "glm"))

The resulting training outcomes by landmark and fitted coefficients are:

training |>
  count(landmark_day, outcome)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   landmark_day outcome     n
#>          <int>   <int> <int>
#> 1            2       0   341
#> 2            2       1    79
#> 3            7       0   336
#> 4            7       1    61
#> 5           14       0   332
#> 6           14       1    34
round(stats::coef(model), 3)
#>    (Intercept)     age_scaled         acuity   signal_as_of days_remaining 
#>         -4.741          0.177          0.510          0.512          0.095

The model uses the days remaining and includes the post-discharge signal only once it is available to the hospital. A death before a possible later readmission prevents that readmission from counting as the outcome. If both events occur at the same time, the example counts the readmission first, as the platform does. Harbor General’s current encounters were not training cases; their outcomes do not enter the fitted model or serve as a performance evaluation.

Supply the hospital’s risk provider

After the platform determines which episodes are eligible, readmit asks the hospital’s risk provider for one estimate per eligible episode. Each request identifies the episode, assessment time, and fixed follow-up endpoint. The provider reads private source information and the saved model from its own project directory. For E4, it reports that age is unavailable; it does not invent a probability. The platform keeps E4 in the eligible population and records the model’s failure. The hospital is responsible for its predictors, their timing, and the suitability of its model; readmit does not validate those choices.

Show risk-provider implementation 
provider_code <- r"---(
rrp_calculate_risk <- function(project_root, request) {
  source_dir <- file.path(project_root, "source")
  patients <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "patients.rds"))
  encounters <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "encounters.rds"))
  observations <- readRDS(file.path(source_dir, "observations.rds"))

  patient <- patients[patients$patient_id == request$patient_id, , drop = FALSE]
  encounter <- encounters[
    encounters$encounter_id == request$index_encounter_id, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(patient) != 1L || is.na(patient$age[[1L]])) {
    return(list(failure = "Patient age unavailable"))
  }
  if (nrow(encounter) != 1L) {
    return(list(failure = "Encounter unavailable"))
  }
  available <- observations[
    observations$encounter_id == request$index_encounter_id &
      observations$available_at <= request$as_of_time, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  signal_as_of <- if (nrow(available)) {
    available$signal[[which.max(available$available_at)]]
  } else {
    0L
  }
  newdata <- data.frame(
    age_scaled = (patient$age[[1L]] - 65) / 10,
    acuity = encounter$acuity[[1L]],
    signal_as_of = signal_as_of,
    days_remaining = request$remaining_seconds / (24 * 60 * 60)
  )
  model <- readRDS(file.path(project_root, "model", "landmark-glm.rds"))
  probability <- as.numeric(stats::predict(model, newdata, type = "response"))
  list(probability = probability)
}
)---"
writeLines(provider_code, file.path(project, "R", "calculate-risk.R"))
rrp_project_validate(project)

Validation confirms that the project files and function signatures load. It does not call either function or certify the simulated clinical definitions, model, or predictions. The following real runs exercise those interfaces.

Assess repeatedly and inspect history

The four assessments use January 6, 10, 12, and 16 as their assessment dates. On January 6, E3, E6, and E7 have not been discharged, so the mapper does not supply them yet. On January 10, E1’s January 9 readmission has already occurred, so E1 no longer receives a risk estimate. E2 remains eligible until its death occurs later. More discharges enter the assessed group over time, while readmissions, deaths, and closed follow-up windows remove episodes from the eligible pool.

At the January 10 assessment, four episodes receive accepted probabilities. E4 remains eligible, but its missing age prevents the model from producing an estimate; the run records one provider failure. For other eligible episodes, the estimated probability may change because the remaining period is shorter and new hospital-owned observations may become available.

stopifnot(nrow(jan10_e1) == 1L,
          jan10_e1$disposition == "known_readmission",
          jan10_e1$terminal_occurred_at == current_events$occurred_at[[1L]],
          !"terminal_available_at" %in% names(history))
history |>
  filter(patient_id %in% c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4")) |>
  select(patient_id, as_of_time, disposition, probability,
         terminal_occurred_at) |>
  arrange(patient_id, as_of_time) |>
  head(22)

Each run adds its episode results to history. E1’s January 6 estimate remains there; its January 10 row instead records the readmission and when it occurred. Earlier rows are not rewritten when a later assessment finds that an event has occurred. E4’s row records that the model could not produce an estimate, not a zero-risk result.

After the January 16 assessment, we run the January 10 assessment again as a historical backfill. It receives a new run ID, and history keeps both January 10 runs. Project status identifies this backfill as the most recently recorded run. Its assessment date is still January 10, so it is not the latest assessment snapshot. The products below select the January 16 run.

We can independently compare E3’s latest accepted probability with a direct prediction from the saved model. E3’s observation is available by January 16.

e3_time <- assessment_times[[4L]]
e3 <- current_encounters |> filter(encounter_id == "E3")
e3_age <- current_patients$age[current_patients$patient_id == "C3"]
e3_expected <- as.numeric(stats::predict(
  readRDS(model_path),
  newdata = data.frame(
    age_scaled = (e3_age - 65) / 10,
    acuity = e3$acuity,
    signal_as_of = current_observations$signal[
      current_observations$encounter_id == "E3"
    ],
    days_remaining = as.numeric(difftime(
      e3$discharge_time + 30 * day, e3_time, units = "days"
    ))
  ),
  type = "response"
))
e3_recorded <- history |>
  filter(episode_id == "episode-E3", as_of_time == e3_time) |>
  pull(probability)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(e3_recorded, e3_expected)))
tibble(recorded = e3_recorded, direct_model_prediction = e3_expected)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   recorded direct_model_prediction
#>      <dbl>                   <dbl>
#> 1   0.0864                  0.0864

Generate and interpret the products

rrp_refresh_products() creates three CSV views from retained history. It does not call the hospital’s source mapper or model again. “Current” means the completed run with the latest assessment date, which is January 16 here. The January 10 backfill ran last but does not replace that snapshot.

If a later-dated run assessed only part of the relevant discharge population, that partial run would still become the current snapshot. The platform does not fill in its missing episodes from older runs. An operational mapper should therefore supply the complete relevant population each time.

products <- rrp_refresh_products(project)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpvLer9x/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
stopifnot(products$selected_run_id == runs[[4L]]$run_id,
          status$latest_run_id == backfill$run_id)
current_risk <- read.csv(products$files[["current_risk"]])
trajectory <- read.csv(products$files[["trajectory"]])
scope <- read.csv(products$files[["scope"]])
current_risk |>
  select(episode_id, disposition, probability)
#>   episode_id      disposition probability
#> 1 episode-E3         accepted  0.08636031
#> 2 episode-E4 provider_failure          NA
#> 3 episode-E6         accepted  0.15285487
#> 4 episode-E7         accepted  0.27509739
#> 5 episode-E8         accepted  0.04086488
trajectory |>
  filter(episode_id == "episode-E3") |>
  select(episode_id, as_of_time, probability)
#>   episode_id                  as_of_time probability
#> 1 episode-E3 2026-01-10T12:00:00.000000Z  0.09088792
#> 2 episode-E3 2026-01-10T12:00:00.000000Z  0.09088792
#> 3 episode-E3 2026-01-12T12:00:00.000000Z  0.12130465
#> 4 episode-E3 2026-01-16T12:00:00.000000Z  0.08636031
scope |>
  select(episodes_assessed, eligible_count, accepted_count,
         provider_failure_count, known_readmission_count,
         known_death_count, window_closed_count)
#>   episodes_assessed eligible_count accepted_count provider_failure_count
#> 1                 8              5              4                      1
#>   known_readmission_count known_death_count window_closed_count
#> 1                       1                 1                   1

Current remaining risk shows episodes still eligible in the January 16 snapshot. E4 remains in this pool even though its probability is missing. E1 and E2 are absent because their readmission and death have occurred; E5’s 30-day window has closed.

Remaining-risk trajectory contains accepted estimates recorded across runs for episodes in the current pool. E3’s rows include both January 10 runs. Each point is an estimate actually recorded at an assessment, not a continuous curve or proof that the patient’s underlying risk changed between assessments.

Operational scope counts all eight episodes in the January 16 assessment: four accepted estimates, one provider failure, and three ineligible outcomes. The CSVs are views derived from history; history retains the completed runs.

Explore and customize the project app

The project app already existed before the first assessment and could have opened with empty views. After product refresh, it reads the three CSVs. Current Risk Pool shows eligible episodes with accepted estimates and E4’s unavailable estimate; selecting a row shows its current estimate and recorded accepted estimates across runs. Overview summarizes the selected assessment and the available current probabilities.

These are separate actions: rrp_run() performs a new assessment and adds history; rrp_refresh_products() updates the CSV views from history; and Reload Data in the app rereads those CSVs. Reloading the app does not run the model or refresh the products.

Install shiny, bslib, reactable, plotly, and yaml in the environment that will run the app. Launch it manually with the following command; the article does not launch an interactive session while rendering.

shiny::runApp(file.path(project, "app"))

Harbor General can replace its project logo without changing the package. We generate a simple PNG in the exact path named by the project’s _brand.yml. Then we append one small color rule to the project-owned stylesheet; the shared package template is untouched. These are examples of ownership, not a new customization framework.

logo_path <- file.path(project, "assets", "project-logo.png")
grDevices::png(logo_path, width = 520, height = 150, bg = "white")
graphics::plot.new()
graphics::rect(0, 0, 1, 1, col = "#174D58", border = NA)
graphics::text(0.5, 0.53, "HARBOR GENERAL", col = "white",
               cex = 1.8, font = 2)
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_png 
#>       2

css_path <- file.path(project, "app", "www", "rrp.css")
cat("\n/* Harbor General project styling */\n",
    ".rrp-page-intro h1 { color: #174D58; }\n",
    file = css_path, append = TRUE)
stopifnot(file.exists(logo_path), file.info(logo_path)$size > 0,
          grepl("assets/project-logo.png", readLines(file.path(project, "_brand.yml")),
                fixed = TRUE) |> any(),
          grepl("Harbor General project styling", readLines(css_path),
                fixed = TRUE) |> any())

For a hosted app, Posit Connect or Posit Connect Cloud are possible deployment choices. The deployment would need the app’s runtime packages, this project’s app, assets, model, and generated products. The hospital also needs a deliberate way to retain project history and run assessments separately from app hosting; the app only reads products. This walkthrough does not deploy or validate a production service.
